AirTag is a great tool for protecting and tracking luggage, but attaching it to smaller devices like cameras can be tricky.

Some people put an AirTag in a regular protective case and clip it to the camera strap, but this method isn't very discreet — a thief can easily spot it and remove it. Fortunately, there are better ways...

Apple has always stressed that the main purpose of AirTag is not for anti-theft. Due to anti-stalking safeguards, a thief will eventually receive a notification that an AirTag is present. However, before that alert appears, you still have several hours to track your belongings, which is why many people use AirTags for this purpose.

Of course, if a thief can quickly locate the AirTag and toss it away, that window of time disappears. That's why regular protective cases, while cheap and easy to install, are easily spotted by thieves.

Fortunately, there are more discreet ways to mount an AirTag on a DSLR or mirrorless camera.

Camera strap clips

The most basic method is using a camera strap clip. These accessories look just like part of the camera strap itself, and if you use a black strap — especially a thicker, padded one — it becomes even more inconspicuous.

Quick-release plates

Photographers often leave a tripod quick-release plate permanently attached to the camera for fast mounting and unmounting throughout the day. There are quick-release plates on the market with built-in AirTag slots that don't draw much attention.

Tripod adapters

If you can't find a quick-release plate compatible with your tripod, another option is to use a universal adapter.

Cages

If you use a camera cage to mount accessories, you can choose a model with a built-in hidden AirTag slot, or purchase a standalone case that attaches to the cage. The latter might not look very discreet on its own, but once mounted on an already accessory-laden cage, it won't stand out.

L-brackets

The latest option is the Peak Design Field Bracket. This L-bracket lets you mount the camera on a tripod in either landscape or portrait orientation, and comes with optional hand straps and a cheese plate for expanding your rig. Instead of an AirTag, it has a built-in tracker compatible with Find My.

Have you tried any of the methods above, or thought of other solutions? Share them in the comments.
